name: Argentine Republic

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 2,780,400 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 2,736,690 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Excludes the Antarctic claim and the Falkland Islands (not in ne:ARG).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 45,851,378). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:ARG.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 p.409 as quoted: 83,000 active (excludes 31,250 paramilitary Gendarmeria/Prefectura). CIA Factbook 2025: ~75,000 (45,000 Army, 15,000 Navy incl. ~3,500 marines, 15,000 Air Force), low.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 as quoted lists no organized reserve (0). High is an educated allowance for recent volunteer leavers recallable within 30 days.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 83,000 (IISS 2024) minus infantry P roles (2,500 + 11,500). Covers navy and air force, armour/artillery crews, logistics and staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to 1982 Falklands/Malvinas mobilization (conscript classes recalled, ~0.5% of population) scaled up for total war; no conscription since 1994 and no organized reserve (IISS). Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry regiments of the armoured brigades on TAM VCTP and M113 (regiments are battalion-sized and understrength). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Argentine_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: TAM VCTP and M113 are 1970s-80s vehicles.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band: all-volunteer force since 1994 but chronic underfunding (~0.5% of GDP) limits exercises, flying hours and sea days.

count.note: Educated guess. Mountain, jungle, airborne and motorized infantry regiments plus ~2,500 marines of the Infanteria de Marina. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Argentine_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: dated personal equipment and night-vision.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: mountain and commando units well trained; others limited by budget.

count.note: Equipment list (IISS as cited): TAM 250 incl. variants (being upgraded to TAM 2C-A2) + SK-105 Kurassier light tanks 112 = 362. Low reflects poor serviceability and the variants included in 250.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: TAM is a 1980s medium tank (105 mm); SK-105 light tank.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band: all-volunteer force since 1994 but chronic underfunding (~0.5% of GDP) limits exercises, flying hours and sea days.

count.note: TAM VCTP 139 + M113 388 + M577 ~20 + Mowag Grenadier ~60 + Stryker M1126 8 (235 on order, Aug 2026) = 615.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: old fleet, Stryker only arriving.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band: all-volunteer force since 1994 but chronic underfunding (~0.5% of GDP) limits exercises, flying hours and sea days.

count.note: TAM VCA 155 mm SP 20 + CITER 155 mm L33 108 + OTO Mod 56 105 mm 64 + CP-30 MLRS 20 + Pampero 5 = 217. Mortar carriers excluded.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band: all-volunteer force since 1994 but chronic underfunding (~0.5% of GDP) limits exercises, flying hours and sea days.

count.note: Argentine Air Force inventory: F-16A/B Block 15 MLU 12 (+12 on order) ex-Danish; first six delivered Dec 2025, second batch of six followed. Mirage family retired 2015; A-4AR no longer listed.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: F-16 MLU is a capable 4th-generation fighter but the fleet is small and new to the FAA.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: conversion still under way, low flying hours.

count.note: Pampa III 11 (4 on order) + EMB-312 Tucano 12 (attack/trainer) = 23. Pampa II trainers excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: light jet trainers and turboprops.

count.note: Army: UH-1H 44 + Bell 212 1 + AS332 1 + SA315 5 + Bell 206 20 + Bell 407 3 = 74 (equipment list); Air Force: Bell 212/412 13 + Bell 407 1 + MD 500 8 + Lama 5 + S-70/S-76 3 = 30 (Argentine Air Force article); Navy ~10 (Sea King, Fennec), educated count. Total ~110.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band: all-volunteer force since 1994 but chronic underfunding (~0.5% of GDP) limits exercises, flying hours and sea days.

count.note: Educated guess. No Group 2+ UAV in Army/Air Force lists beyond small Mavic/Tehuelche types; mid allows for Navy/FAA trials. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Argentine_Army)
Active ships list: Almirante Brown-class (MEKO 360H2, classed destroyers, frigate-sized) 3; Heroina retired 2024. Convention: ships_major = destroyers + frigates.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: 1983 ships with old Exocet MM38/Aspide.

count.note: Espora-class corvettes 6 (Parker inactive mid-2025) + Gowind OPVs 4 + King 1 + Intrepida 2 + Baradero/Punta Mogotes/Zurubi patrol boats 7 = 20; amphibious support ship excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: Gowind OPVs modern but lightly armed.

count.note: Active ships list: as of 2025 the entire submarine fleet is inactive (Santa Cruz and Salta in reserve). High allows for a reactivated boat.

training.note: Rubric 0.25: no submarine sea time since 2017 (San Juan loss).

count.note: Equipment list: Oerlikon GDF 35 mm 38 + Bofors 40 mm 24 guns with 5 Skyguard fire-control units, RBS 70 NG MANPADS (classified number); ~9 batteries (educated conversion, ~6 guns per battery).

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band: all-volunteer force since 1994 but chronic underfunding (~0.5% of GDP) limits exercises, flying hours and sea days.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: competent staff schools; 1982 combat experience is now institutional memory only; joint command weak.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: volunteer professionals with strong Malvinas-era identity, but low pay and retention problems.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 average; higher in a South Atlantic/sovereignty scenario.

weapons.note: Below anchor 9: few modern guided weapons; F-16 brings AIM-9/AIM-120-class only if supplied.

armor.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: TAM (1980s, 105 mm, no composite armour), Stryker arriving.

ships.note: Below anchor 9: MEKO 360/140 1980s, no operational submarines; Gowind OPVs modern.

logistics.note: Below anchor 9: small airlift (5 C-130H, KC-130H), rail freight, limited sealift.

communications.note: Near anchor 9: ARSAT satellites (civil), limited tactical data links.

isr.note: Below anchor 9: SAOCOM radar satellites (civil/dual-use), P-3C Orion (ex-Norway), INVAP radars.

air.note: Anchor 9: F-16A/B MLU (1980s airframe, MLU avionics).

cyber.note: Below anchor 10: Joint Cyber Defence Command (2014), small.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 1,022,082,332,049 / population 45,851,378 = 22,291 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 1,276,804,911,991 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,022,082,332,049 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ARG/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 0.56% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 0.5% (2023), 0.6% (2024); among the lowest in the region.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 22.87% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Among the largest net food exporters per capita (soy meal, maize, wheat, beef); not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 22,763,219 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 8.115% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 369,469. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. FAdeA Cordoba builds the IA-63 Pampa III at a low rate. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Air_Force)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. TAM line (TAMSE) closed; upgrades only; small wheeled vehicle assembly. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Argentine_Army)

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Tandanor/Rio Santiago shipyards; patrol boats only. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Argentine_Navy_ships)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 240,000 km total (2017), 81,355 km paved, 4,423 km controlled-access. Mid is paved plus half the unpaved network (derived midpoint); high is the total.

railKm.note: World Bank 17,866 km (2019; CIA Factbook same, 2018). High allows for the nominal network incl. lines out of service (educated).

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 37 ports, 1 large + 2 medium + 10 small; 13 key ports named (Buenos Aires, Rosario, Bahia Blanca/Ingeniero White, Puerto Belgrano, Mar del Plata, Puerto Madryn, Ushuaia...). Mid adds the main river ports of the Parana (educated).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Argentina is below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-fleet table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country); CIA Factbook 2023 counts 201 merchant ships (33 tankers, few cargo ships).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck-based sustainment; long Patagonian distances with few roads.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (~2.5 million) and mules; not from FAO data. Mountain units use mules.

nuclearWarheads.note: Argentina is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Party to Tlatelolco and ABACC with Brazil; civilian nuclear industry (INVAP).

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Andes and Patagonian depth, population support; Patagonia is harsh but sparsely defended.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:ARG (World Bank); the Falkland/Malvinas Islands and the Antarctic claim are not inside the border. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2024 (personnel) as quoted; Argentine Army equipment list, Argentine Air Force article (F-16 deliveries Dec 2025 onward) and the active Argentine Navy ships list. ships_major = destroyers/frigates; ships_minor = corvettes, OPVs, patrol boats; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Gendarmeria and Prefectura (paramilitary) excluded. Serviceability is low across all services (budget ~0.5% of GDP).
